clips.transcript: I can show you around. If you'd like a tour, tap me now, and I will guide you through the galleries. You can always walk around using the controls.
Before we start: you can always walk around with the controls while I'm talking. When it's time for the next stop, I'll bring you along.

Welcome. I'm so glad you're here.
These are paintings by TJ Murphy, an artist based in Seattle.
In his words: "I first started painting from sitting on the beach at Denny Blaine and sketching Mount Rainier."
He did a bunch of pen and ink sketches.
Then he picked up watercolor, to try and capture the luminosity of the light in the sky.
In 2020 he got more serious about it. He had some time, and started doing bigger work.
Come with me. We'll start with the mountain, where it all began.

Here's Rainier over the lake at sunrise, seen from Denny Blaine, near TJ's home.
That's TJ on the rocks, wrapped in his meditation blanket.
His friend Lisa brought it back from Tanzania, on his birthday. Red and blue Maasai cloth.
Now this one. The blanket's still there, but TJ has disappeared.
In his words: "It's still a self-portrait. I'm just not in it. I'm everything in it."

Most mornings he sits out on his balcony before dawn, in that same blanket.
Next, somewhere much warmer.

Welcome to El Salvador.
These Atami sunsets are from TJ's first visit, in 2022.
This one is a sunset in El Zonte, from 2023.
He stayed at a hostel on the corner where the river meets the beach.
He woke before dawn to meditate and watch the light come.
The surfers were already paddling out, and the big round stones tumbled with every wave.
The tropical air makes the light especially luminous.

He painted that one later, in his Seattle studio, from photos he took on the trip.
Now, from places to family.

On this wall, side by side, are TJ's dad and mom.
This is his dad, Paul Murphy.
They've been painting together since COVID. His dad picked up a brush shortly after TJ did, for the first time in his life.
TJ also illustrated twelve poems for his dad's book, Reflections on Time.
And his dad gave him a bass he bought the Christmas TJ got a guitar, at about eight, and never really played.
His dad said, "I think that bass is a lot happier with you."
And this is his mom, Ruth.
He painted her while they were hanging out at her house in Florida. She has a beautiful smile and bright eyes.

And this is TJ's grandfather, Howard.
TJ painted it for Grandpa Howard's memorial, and made one for each of Howard's children, as a gift to remember him by.
Howard was a saintly man, and a true follower of Jesus.
Every year he went on mission trips to Costa Rica, where he built schools and helped the indigenous community build what they needed.
He was peaceful, calm, and patient. A true example.

TJ's usual medium these days is watercolor pastel.
Through here, you may recognize a few faces, if you know Bitcoin.

These are the Bitcoiners.
In TJ's words: "When I started going to Bitcoin conferences, I did a bunch of portraits of the speakers as a conversation starter."
"I've handed probably 20 or 30 out, and it's got me invited to some fun parties."
And over here is Ser at Pacific Bitcoin Festival.

TJ's paintings are full of the people in his life.
His friend Craig came down to the beach and took the photos for his self-portrait.

In 2023 he went kayaking with friends out to Sucia and Patos.
His first time in an ocean kayak. The current nearly pulled them to the other island.
He calls it humbling. And beautiful.

clips.section: Walk: Friends to the Friends Club mural
clips.transcript:
Let's head out to the courtyard for our last stop.
It's a big one. You can't miss it.

This is the Friends Club mural, a 40 by 9 foot shipping container in Lillooet, British Columbia.
TJ met Kara and Paul, who organize the Friends Club festival, at a Provibers reunion in 2026.
Nearing three in the morning, Kara asked, "Do you do murals?"
He'd done one, some twenty years earlier.
He painted this one as a gift, because he likes these people.
Ed the Spaceman floats down the river on a raft, with Tobias the dog and Billy Buff the chin-man.
The Lady on the right points him to the festival on the far hill.
In TJ's words: "We trusted in each other, and what emerged was magnificent."
That's the end of our tour. Thank you so much for walking with me.
Original paintings and portrait commissions are available through Vermillion Aurora Productions.
Feel free to keep exploring. I'll be right here if you need me.
